harness.docs: scripts/kaggle/README.md (scripts/cloud/README.md marks the old driver historical)
harness.engine: transformers through campaign_eval (development_evaluator for DEV panels, batched_greedy_generate for prompt files, plus seeded sampling with k samples). vLLM not used: the gates and baseline are bound to the evaluator's batching (batch 32, length-descending order, left pad 1, dynamic cache), batch composition alone moves bf16 outputs (54% identity batch 1 vs 32), and vLLM's continuous batching cannot reproduce it.
harness.work_split: whole global batches: batch b -> shard b % shard_count -> worker j % workers; --workers 2 runs both T4s as independent processes
harness.code_delivery: GitHub codeload tarball at the pushed commit, checked against a sha256 digest of packages/sepalith/src and infer_entry.py computed from git by the driver
harness.secrets: none in the kernel (the driver refuses token-like strings); public HF reads need no token; uploads (--upload-hf) run on the PC with the hf login. Kaggle CLI 2.2.4 authenticates with KAGGLE_API_TOKEN (KGAT_) from the environment; the driver reads it from ~/.config/sepalith/secrets.env into the CLI subprocess only.
harness.quota: kaggle quota before and after each run; push refused (exit 3) if used + estimate > 20 GPU-h; ledger ~/.local/state/sepalith/kaggle/quota-ledger.jsonl

Static batches run until their longest row ends; gate 268 hits the cap on 8% of DEV250 rows, so nearly every 32-row batch runs to 1,024 steps. question_for_user: With the bound-batching transformers path, Kaggle T4s generate about 106 tokens/s per two-T4 session, so the C12 census (15,006 prompts x 8 samples, cap 1,024) projects to about 67 to 133 Kaggle GPU-hours, or 3 to 7 weeks of the 20 GPU-hour R7 budget. Which way should C12 go? Recommended: allow one bounded Kaggle trial (at most 1 GPU-hour) of vLLM with CUDA graphs and continuous batching for the census only. It would get its own fp16 parity check against the same bf16 references; the bound-batching path stays the parity and evaluation reference. If vLLM cannot reach about 5x, reduce the census (for example 4 samples and cap 512). Colab free has the same T4 class and does not change the arithmetic.
notes: Harness, smoke and parity tooling are done; the card's parity receipt waits for the night reference job. The parent pre-check (57% identity, cap +3) does not meet the card's 90%/within-1 criteria, but it measures run-on drift: the PC's own bf16 batch-1 vs batch-32 identity is 54%. The representative check is the SFT checkpoint, whose outputs are short (median 26 tokens on DEV75). Kaggle can only read it if its weights are made readable there, for example a private Kaggle dataset (the user said not to upload it anywhere today), or by running parity on the arm-A model once R8 publishes it. fp32 fallback: weights alone are 10 GB in fp32, so batch 32 with DEV75's longest prompts will not fit a T4; an fp32 run would need smaller batches and so different batching than the PC references.
